requirements.text: All documents must include a mandatory status attribute with values of original, copy, revision, or cancellation.
The Party UUID must be a universally unique identifier for an instance of Party.
The Document UUID must be a computer generated unique identifier for the Document.
The Document ID must be the Document identifier within the sender's system.
The Document Date must be the date or date/time assigned to the Document by the sender.
The Document Status must be included in all documents.
The Test Status must be a boolean indicating if the document is for test purposes.
The Sender Software Manufacturer must be identified by a URI.
The Sender Software Product must be the software manufacturer's name for the product.
The Sender Software Version must be the software manufacturer's product version.
The Schema Version must be the version of the XML schema with which the document complies.
The VAT Evidence attribute must indicate whether the invoice can be used for VAT purposes.
The Paid In Full attribute must indicate whether the invoice has already been paid.
The Line UUID must be a unique instance identifier for the line.
The Line Number must be a positive integer starting with 1.
The Line Status must be one of original, revision, or deletion.
The Line Quantity must be the quantity of goods or services on a line.
The Amount Ex VAT must be the monetary amount excluding VAT on the line.
The Item Name must be in a form mutually understood by both Buyer and Seller.
The Unit of Measure must be a code describing the quantity in which goods and services are priced.
The Unit Price must include a currency code expressed using ISO 4217 3-character codes.
The Commodity Class must use UNSPSC or another classification agreed with OGC.
The Extended Item ID must be any part number other than the Seller Item ID or GTIN.
The Extended Item ID Source must specify the origin of the Extended Item ID.
The Aspect Name must be the name of the aspect.
The Aspect Value must be the value of the aspect.
The Aspect Value Unit must be the unit associated with the aspect value.
The Requested Delivery Date is mandatory for RFQ documents.
The Quoted Delivery Date is mandatory for Quotation documents.
The Required By Date is mandatory for Purchase Order documents.
The Rectification Action is mandatory for Rectification Advice documents.

Define the minimum cryptographic standards for the Digital Signature, including required algorithms (e.g., RSA-SHA256 or higher), key length, and the requirement for a secure PKI or certificate validation process.
The Document ID must be a string of up to 35 alphanumeric characters, consistent with standard EDI/XML interoperability practices.
Item Name must be a string of exactly 70 characters; if the name is shorter, it must be padded with trailing spaces, and if longer, it must be truncated.
Define maximum allowed XML message size (e.g., 5MB) and maximum processing latency for document validation and parsing (e.g., < 500ms per document).
Specify that the generation and validation of UUIDs must not exceed a specific latency threshold (e.g., < 10ms) to ensure it does not impact high-throughput message processing.

OPEN: The specification includes sensitive financial data (e.g., Bank Account Numbers, Sort Codes, Purchase Card details) but lacks requirements for data protection, encryption at rest, or secure handling of PII/financial identifiers. - All documents containing sensitive financial identifiers (Bank Account, Card Number, CVV) must be encrypted at rest and in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher, and access to these fields must be restricted based on the principle of least privilege.

OPEN: The specification mentions 'Digital Signature' but does not define the required cryptographic standards (e.g., algorithm, key length) or the handling of validation failures. - All documents must support W3C XML Digital Signatures using RSA-SHA256 or higher, and the receiver must reject documents with invalid signatures.

OPEN: The specification requires a 'Schema Version' but does not define a versioning strategy or how to handle backward compatibility between different schema versions. - The Schema Version must follow Semantic Versioning (Major.Minor.Patch); receiving systems must support at least one previous Major version for backward compatibility.

OPEN: The PRD mentions 'large scale' but provides no metrics on expected transaction volume, concurrent users, or peak load requirements. - Specify expected peak throughput (e.g., 'The system must support 10,000 transactions per hour') to allow implementers to design for appropriate capacity.
